paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the changes in Efficacy_top and noise_E with the number of edits for GPT2-XL, comparing AlphaEdit and MEMIT. The x-axis represents the number of edits, ranging from 0 to 3000 in increments of 500 on a linear scale, labeled as "Number of Edits". The y-axis on the left, labeled "Efficacy_top", ranges from 30 to 100 in increments of 10, while the y-axis on the right, labeled "noise_E", ranges from 0 to 140 in increments of 20. For AlphaEdit, the Efficacy_top (dashed red line with square markers) starts at approximately 100 and gradually decreases to around 85 at 3000 edits, while noise_E (solid red line with circular markers) remains relatively flat, increasing slightly from about 10 to 20. For MEMIT, Efficacy_top (dashed light blue line with square markers) begins at approximately 90 and declines sharply to around 20 at 3000 edits, whereas noise_E (solid light blue line with circular markers) increases steadily from about 10 to 140. The plot uses a dual y-axis to display both metrics simultaneously, with gridlines for clarity.
